subject: physics
question_text: A vector V makes an angle with the horizontal. The vector is rotated through an angle α. Does this rotation change the vector V?

verification.note: Sri Chaitanya IPE Junior Fastrack (Rev. May 2024), VERY SHORT ANSWER 2 of Unit 4. The mark split is invented and needs a Telangana IPE teacher; no exam appearance years are printed for Unit 4, so appearances[] stays empty.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: What stays the same
lines: Rotation does not change the length of
the vector, so its magnitude |V| stays
steps.margin_note: Say magnitude FIRST — it is the half the examiner checks you did not forget.
steps.why: A rotation turns a vector without stretching it, so the size cannot change. Only the direction is in question.
common_mistakes: Claiming the magnitude changes with the angle.

recall.must_convey: That the magnitude stays the same under rotation.

steps.memory_tip: Turn a pencil on the table. Its length does not change, only the way it points.

steps.label: What changes
lines: The direction changes for every α that
A vector is its magnitude AND direction,

lines.text: so yes — the vector V is changed.

steps.margin_note: The exception matters: a full turn brings the direction back, so only then is V unchanged.
steps.why: Direction is half of what a vector is. Change the direction and the vector is a different vector, even at the same length.
common_mistakes: Answering "no change" because the magnitude is the same.

recall.must_convey: That the direction changes (except full turns), so V is changed.
accept: direction changes so the vector changes

steps.memory_tip: The components change as well: V cos θ and V sin θ both take new values after the turn.

insider_note: The answer is yes, and the two marks split across what stays and what changes. Writing only "the magnitude is unchanged" scores one.
